name: BANGLADESH

flag.title: Flag of Bangladesh
flag.note: Green field, red disc offset to centre

lead: Bangladesh is a flat, low land. Three great rivers fan out here into the world's largest delta (land built by rivers). More people live here than in Russia, in a country smaller than England. Tigers swim in the Sundarbans, the biggest mangrove forest on Earth. Rice fields turn bright green every monsoon (rainy season).

sections.wows: 7 things to make you go wow

geo: Bangladesh sits on a giant river delta, crisscrossed by over 700 rivers. Every monsoon, floods cover a third of the land. They leave fertile mud for farming.
The Sundarbans, a forest of salt-water mangrove trees, lies in the south-west, on the border with India. It covers 10,200 km² and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
animals: The Royal Bengal tiger is the national animal. About 125 live in the Sundarbans. They swim between islands through salty channels.
The hilsa (ilish) is the national fish. Fishers say hilsa from the Padma River taste the best.
culture: The poet Rabindranath Tagore, born in this region, wrote thousands of songs. One poem became the national anthem. At Pahela Baishakh, the spring festival, streets fill with orange-and-white clothes.
Dhaka is famous for Jamdani weaving. Weavers make shimmering muslin, a fine cloth, from memory. Bangladesh is also the world's second-largest maker of clothes for other countries.
history: For centuries this was the heart of Bengal, a wealthy land of rice and muslin. Mughal (Indian) emperors and British traders both wanted it. British rule slowly drained its wealth.
In 1971, Bangladesh fought a nine-month Liberation War against Pakistan. Victory came on 16 December, now Victory Day. It is one of the world's youngest nations.
wows: Bangladesh has the world's largest river delta, where the Ganges and Brahmaputra meet the sea.
Sundarbans tigers swim and hunt in salty water, as no other tigers do.
Bangladesh supplies 86% of the world's hilsa fish.
Dhaka has about 44,000 people per km², one of Earth's most crowded cities.
Mughal emperors called Dhaka muslin 'woven air'.
The 6.15 km Padma Bridge, finished in 2022, used only Bangladesh's own money.
Poet Tagore's poems became the national anthems of two nations, Bangladesh and India.

myths.fact: Cox's Bazar, a seaside town, has about 120 km of unbroken sand, often called the world's longest sea beach.

myths.myth: Bangladesh is one of the poorest countries
myths.fact: Millions of people there have left poverty since 1990.
